summary.headline: Awfis Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR425 crores and cash EBITDA reached INR44 crores, while blended occupancy held flat at 76%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 27% YoY to INR425 crores and reported EBITDA rose 28% to INR162 crores (38.2% margin), with PBT of INR24 crores. Management introduced cash EBITDA as a new metric: INR44 crores (10.1% margin), up about 34% YoY. Occupancy was flat at 76% QoQ, though the mature cohort dipped to 83% from 84% after one enterprise client with about 3,000 seats across five centres exited. Management guided to FY27 cash EBITDA of INR190-200 crores, with H2 expected to outperform H1.

segments.name: Co-working and allied services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR352 crores, up 27% YoY. GCCs contribute 24% of rental revenue from 100+ unique GCC clients across nine cities.

segments.name: Transform (construction and fit-out)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR73 crores, up 25% YoY. Third-party share about 92% this quarter; management says blended margin is around 17-18% (15% on landlord-partner work, 18-20% on third-party). Over 200 crores of mandates won for FY27.

guidance_outlook: Co-working revenue growth of 23-25% YoY for FY27.
Transform growth of about 20%; total FY27 revenue to exceed INR1,800 crores.
FY27 cash EBITDA of INR190-200 crores, with H2 better than H1 and Q4 expected to show a meaningful improvement in occupancy and margins.
FY27 capex of roughly INR200-210 crores.
Premium mix expected to move from about 85:15 to about 80:20 by end FY27, as about 10 of 13 pipeline properties are premium (Gold/Elite).
capex_capacity: Operational seats about 159,000 across 242 centres in 18 cities; 9 centres under fit-out (total 251); pipeline of 267 centres including LOIs.
Total capacity including fit-out about 170,000 seats; including signed LOIs over 185,000 seats.
Q1 gross seat additions about 4,600 against about 1,800 seats exited in portfolio consolidation.

Malpani Estates developer partnership (Pune, two Grade A+ assets, 1.4 lakh sq ft). Developer partnership centres expected to go live in 9-15 months; company contributes about 50% of fit-out value upfront as a security deposit; 9-year agreements.
Seven premium properties in the portfolio (two live, five under construction), priced 30-50% above the existing portfolio. Elite centres rose from 8 to 10; Gold held at 27.
Management expects over 12,000 seats on track in H1 FY27 across the three multiformat pillars.
demand_pricing: Active clients over 3,600; corporates and MNCs about 64% of base. Weighted average client tenure 38 months; average lock-in 26 months.
Mix by sector: technology 39%, professional services 21%, BFSI 13%, manufacturing 12%, healthcare and life sciences 5%. Domicile: 52% India-headquartered, 43% North American or European.
Clients with 500+ seats make up 37% of portfolio. Q1 sold 13,000 seats.
Blended occupancy 76% (flat QoQ); mature cohort (over 12 months old) 83%, down from 84%.
Pricing: 4-7% contractual escalation within same client; management says price per seat has risen every quarter over eight quarters. No exact figure given.
Replacement of vacated capacity: significant part pre-committed, some at higher pricing than the exited client paid.
Industry: H1 2026 flex leasing 8.4 million sq ft (+55%); GCC leasing 16.5 million sq ft (+38%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did rental payments jump from about INR85 crores in Q4 to about INR130 crores in Q1, and is the company shifting toward straight lease?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the cash-flow rent figure excludes rent booked in other expenses (MA profit shares and out-of-lock-in leases not under Ind AS 116); that line was flat, so combined growth is in line with indices. Management said MA is 57% of current supply (down from 62%), and the mix is opportunistic, not a shift away from MA.

qa_highlights.question: How do developer partnerships work: construction stage at signing, delivery timing, capital contribution and access period?
qa_highlights.answer: Centres could go live 9-15 months after signing. Company contributes about 50% of fit-out value on day one as a security deposit until go-live. Nine-year agreements start at signing, with the nine years counted from OC and possession.

qa_highlights.question: What is per-seat revenue trend given chargeable area growth versus revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 68% vs 65% comparison, because chargeable area includes unlive fit-out seats. Net operational seats rose 59% from about 100,000 to 159,000 against 65% revenue growth. Price per seat rises through 4-7% escalations and premium mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Transform's third-party share about 92%, and what are its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Transform has shifted to third-party work; the 92% reflects this quarter's delivery mix and is expected to stay structurally high. Margins: about 15% on landlord-partner work and 18-20% on third-party, blending to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the implied FY27 cash EBITDA margin only about 10% when occupancy is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the exit of one large client, where the company kept fixed costs on five centres to refill them, and a timing gap of 3-4 quarters between landlord rent resets (many 2021 leases) and customer repricing. H2 is expected to be better, with Q4 showing a meaningful improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio is premium, and is the new supply institutional?
qa_highlights.answer: About 37 of 242 live centres (about 15%) are Gold/premium. Of the 13 properties in LOI or fit-out, about 10 are premium. The premium mix is expected to reach about 80:20 by end FY27. All pipeline assets are institutional.
